name: Riverbottom
description:
Riverbottom is the lowest point in Meridian 88 that isn't underwater. That distinction matters here more than anywhere else, because the water is always coming. The district sits at the absolute southern terminus of the megacity, where the engineered drainage systems that protect the Meridian Core and the Shelf thin out to nothing. When the lake surges or the spring melt overwhelms the pumping stations, Riverbottom floods first and drains last. The old Altgeld Gardens public housing blocks -- themselves a monument to decades of environmental racism in pre-Meridian Chicago -- were rebuilt as Meridian Residential Block South-9, a name so deliberately forgettable it amounts to erasure. The new blocks are identical modular stacks, six stories of poured composite with neural-compatible wiring and nothing else. No common spaces. No green areas. No pretense.

The environmental justice concerns that defined old Riverdale didn't go away when the neighborhood got a new name. They got a corporate rebrand. Three waste processing facilities ring the district, handling chemical reclamation for the southern industrial zone. The air quality index in Riverbottom regularly exceeds Meridian safety thresholds by 200%, but the thresholds are advisory, not mandatory, and advisories don't apply below Tier 3. Residents have filed 14,000 environmental complaints through the Meridian civic interface in the past decade. The system logs them, categorizes them, and routes them to a processing queue that has never, in its operational history, produced a response.

But Riverbottom endures, the way things endure at the bottom of gravity wells -- not by climbing out but by becoming so dense that nothing can compress them further. The community organizing tradition that existed in Altgeld Gardens survived the transition to Meridian, adapted, and hardened. Block councils operate with military discipline, coordinating flood response, air filtration maintenance, and the distribution of smuggled medical supplies for the respiratory conditions the waste plants cause and the corporate health system doesn't cover. There is a saying in Riverbottom: the water rises, and so do we. It's painted on the side of Block South-9 in letters three stories tall. Nobody has tried to remove it.

sights: Identical modular housing stacks stretching in grid formation, brutalist and unadorned
Waste processing facility smokestacks rimming the horizon, exhaust plumes lit amber at night
High-water marks stained on building walls at varying heights -- a flood history written in grime
Community murals on Block South-9 -- defiant, colorful, repainted after every flood
Makeshift levee barriers stored on every block, ready for deployment
sounds: The constant industrial drone of waste processing -- a low frequency hum felt in the chest
Pumping station machinery cycling on and off, the sound of borrowed time
Block council alert sirens -- three tones: flood warning, air quality alert, all clear
Children coughing -- the sound Riverbottom can't escape
smells: Chemical processing byproduct -- metallic, acrid, and inescapable on bad air days
Standing water from the last flood event that hasn't fully drained
Bleach and industrial cleaner from the constant post-flood remediation
Community kitchens cooking with whatever the supply chain delivered this week
atmosphere.feel: Compressed. Riverbottom feels like a place that has been pushed down so many times it has become structurally incapable of surprise. The anger here isn't hot -- it's geological. Layers of grievance compressed into something harder than the composite walls. People don't hope for rescue. They organize for survival.

demographics: Overwhelmingly Tier 1 and untier-ed residents. The legacy Black community from Altgeld Gardens persists alongside environmental refugees and workers displaced from shuttered southern industrial operations. Population approximately 35,000, though flooding events cause periodic displacement.
economy: Waste processing plant employment, block council mutual aid systems, and a surprisingly sophisticated gray market in air filtration components. Some residents earn supplemental income as flood remediation specialists -- skills learned from necessity, marketed to wealthier districts that flood less often.
power_structure: The waste processing facilities are operated by Axiom Environmental Services under sovereign industrial charter, making them functionally immune to local complaint. Block councils hold real authority within the residential stacks, operating as the only functional governance Riverbottom has ever known.
dangers: Flooding -- chronic, recurring, and worsening as climate infrastructure degrades
Toxic air quality from the waste processing ring -- respiratory illness rates are four times the Meridian average
Infrastructure collapse during flood events -- the modular blocks weren't built for water exposure
Axiom Environmental Security patrols protecting plant perimeters with escalation-of-force protocols
Despair -- the most dangerous thing in Riverbottom is the rational conclusion that nothing will change
opportunities: Block council networks are the tightest community infrastructure in southern Meridian -- trust is real here
Environmental data from Riverbottom could be devastating if it reached the right journalist or activist
Flood remediation expertise is genuinely valuable and in demand across the city
The waste plants process materials that occasionally include salvageable tech and rare elements
story_hooks: A block council leader has been compiling environmental health data for twenty years and is ready to release it -- but the last three people who tried to whistleblow on Axiom Environmental are dead or missing
The flood patterns are changing in ways the pumping station data doesn't explain -- someone is diverting drainage capacity away from Riverbottom deliberately
Underneath Block South-9, the original Altgeld Gardens foundation contains a sealed community archive from the pre-Meridian environmental justice movement
frequented_by: Waste processing plant workers on rotating shifts
Block council organizers coordinating flood and air response
Gray market filtration dealers supplying what the health system won't
Environmental data runners carrying readings to contacts outside the district
Nobody from the Spire -- Riverbottom doesn't appear on their maps
